title: Cacio e Pepe
subtitle: Roman pasta with Pecorino Romano and black pepper
excerpt: The simplest and most technically demanding of the great Roman pastas: spaghetti dressed with nothing but Pecorino Romano, Parmesan, and a bold quantity of coarsely ground black pepper.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cacio e pepe (cheese and pepper) is one of the four great Roman pasta dishes, alongside carbonara, amatriciana, and gricia. It is believed to have originated as a dish of the shepherds (pastori) of the Apennines, who carried hard cheeses, dried pasta, and pepper on long drives and prepared this simple dish en route. The recipe has only three main components, which makes the technique critical: the heat of the pasta and a controlled amount of starchy cooking water are the only emulsifiers that bind the cheese into a smooth, coating sauce. Too much heat causes the cheese to clump; too little and the sauce is grainy. The cooking water must be less salted than normal because the Pecorino Romano is very salty. The dish must be served immediately: it does not hold.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the pasta. A wide, deep frying pan or sauté pan for finishing the sauce.

content.text: Use lightly salted water for the pasta: less than usual because the Pecorino Romano is very salty. Toast the black pepper in a dry pan until it becomes fragrant before grinding. Grate the cheese very finely on a microplane or the finest side of a box grater. Mix the cheese with a small amount of cold water to form a paste before adding the pasta water: this pre-hydration prevents clumping. The sauce is finished off the heat. Toss constantly and add pasta water by the tablespoon until a smooth, glossy sauce coats every strand.

content.text: Cook the pasta in lightly salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 300 ml of the pasta cooking water before draining.

Toast the pepper in a wide pan over medium heat for 1 minute until fragrant. Add 100 ml of the pasta water and let it bubble for 30 seconds. Add the drained pasta and toss constantly, adding pasta water a tablespoon at a time to keep the pasta moving.

Remove the pan from the heat. Mix the grated Pecorino and Parmesan with 3 tablespoons of cold pasta water to make a paste. Add to the pan and toss vigorously, adding pasta water as needed until the sauce is smooth and glossy and coats every strand. Serve immediately.
